marketingRemarks.marketingRemark: Charming Character  &  Comfortable Living in a Desirable Merced Neighborhood! Inside, tile flooring flows throughout the main living areas, creating a cohesive feel complemented by an open floor plan. The inviting living room is large and the separate family room features a beamed ceiling and brick fireplace with mantle, adding warmth and character to the space. The remodeled kitchen combines style and functionality with a breakfast bar, cozy nook, recessed lighting, and pantry cabinet. Wood flooring extends into the bedrooms, each offering comfortable space and closets, while the remodeled bathroom features tile flooring, granite countertops, and a tub with shower over, along with a convenient closet. Laundry is located in the garage for added convenience. Outside, a covered patio and wood fenced backyard create a comfortable setting for enjoying time outdoors. Additional features include a raised foundation, siding lap exterior, composition shingle roof, and whole-house fan. Ideally located near shopping, dining, schools, parks, and major roadways, this home offers both everyday convenience and timeless appeal.

schoolReviews.review: Franklin Elementary School is an exceptional institution that excels in nurturing young minds and fostering a love for learning. The dedicated staff members go above and beyond to create a supportive and engaging environment for students. The school's commitment to academic excellence, coupled with a strong emphasis on character development, sets a remarkable standard for education. With a rich array of extracurricular activities and a focus on individualized attention, Franklin Elementary School truly stands out as a beacon of quality education and holistic growth for every child fortunate enough to be a part of its community.

I would never send my children to this school again. We MOVED out of the school district to get out of the environment. It’s run down (I know school finances are tight). Programs/performances ran by the school are rushed and not organized and there’s hardly any room in the cafeteria to be present for awards and programs (get there an hour early and be prepared to be ambushed by the parents coming in for the next students awards. I’ve never been to a school like this and we’ve been in four elementary schools (we move for work.)

I love this school, it's one of the only reasons I want to stay where I live, so both of my kids can go here. I love all the staff and I go to the Parent Teacher Club meetings and it showed me how much the staff really cares for not only the children but all the families, siblings, and parents, and grandparents. They very caring to the needs of all the children and they do a great job of keeping all the kids safe and well taken care of. I love this school. My daughter loves her class, they really keep the kids busy and learning. She has learned so much!

schoolReviews.review: This school is by far worst from what my friends tell me. How does a third grader struggle to learn when the teachers don't teach them the correct way. Using too much technology to make their life easier isn't helping the kids. They don't even know how to use a dictionary book. Their homework is always a struggle for them because they're not taught how to do the homework. It's like throwing things at kids and expect them to learn. The office staffs are so inattentive and rude. Parking lot is chaotic when picking up the kids. Some teachers gives you an attitude when you go pick up your kids. Everyone seems rushed to go home and I feel like the school is all about getting money instead of improving it. No wonder California ranks the bottom in education, no one cares anymore.

Worst school my child has ever attended.. My daughter is in a fourth/fifth grade combo class and has went from a child who loved school to hating it and getting in trouble all the time. Her teacher is moody and depending on her mood is the amount of homework the children will get... My daughter frequently comes home with 2 hr+ of homework. In my opinon is too much. The teachers here love to give detention for EVERYTHING!! My daughter got a detention for forgetting to put her name on a paper... seriously?! Oh and if your child needs to use the restroom... you guessed it.. DETENTION!! Upon asking the principal why this is standard she says that they are teaching them responsiblity.. that if the teachers cant use the restroom during class neither should the children and that they are prepping them for middle school but i'm pretty sure in middle school you don't get detention for bathroom breaks unless you make it a habit. And i'm pretty sure a teacher should be able to hold needing to use the restroom better than a 8 year old!! Teacher parent communication here is a joke i've asked (teachers and vice principal) serveral times to be kept upd on my childs progress and still nothing!

This is our second year at this school. My child is in fourth grade right now and is very frustrated. My child's perception is that the teacher seems to favor girls over boys. He seems to be in trouble all the time for not showing his work and getting detentions for the same reason. He is very discourage and his grades keep getting worse. He has gone from being an excellent student to hating school and not wanting to go.

We have had 2 very organized, structured teachers (3rd and 4th grades). They are nice, and experienced, but they seem to care only about test preparation instead of what the child is ready to learn. In other words, if your kid is a slow learner, too bad. They are still given the same work as the other students and made to feel stressed that the tests are coming up. Areas that might actually motivate a person to learn, such as art, science, history, and music are virtually ignored because the focus is almost entirely on reading, writing and math skills. There is only so much drill these kids can take. My child is hating school because he has trouble finishing the given amount of work in the same time as other students. As a result, he has recess detention almost daily. The school has the same policy if they don't get the homework done. He is discouraged. We work with him at home, but he still struggles. I wish the teachers at this school would help each student develop their own strengths instead of making everyone feel guilty for not fitting in to their desired statistics. When you go to a conference, the teachers do not ask you anything or listen. Too bad.

My daughter is friends with the girl and she tells my daughter that she likes boys yet, she is allowed to change in the boys locker room and how she watches the boys change. My daughter went to this school for 7th and 8th grades. She absolutely loved it! The growth I saw in my child academically and emotionally outweighed any concerns I may have had when we first started with this school. 8th grade was specially great! Mr. Cooper, Mr. Bromfield, Mr. Hart, and Mr. Church pushed my child to excellence. She went from thinking she was a B student to an "A" student. The principal, Mr. Ferguson is very supportive and hands on with students.

I am a student that goes to Rivera. I certainly do not recommend it to any parents to enroll their children to the school. Even though the school academics are great, there is way too much drugs alcohol and violence on this campus. I am hoping to get into Mcswain school for my 8th grade year. I dislike this school with a passion.

schoolReviews.review: The school does a tremendous job of meeting the needs of students despite being a large school.
Honestly how do I even explain this, they have the right ideas but wrong execution

I graduated in 2016. I can attest to the AP curriculum that it is top notch. Common core has tainted the common core curriculum like a virus but that's every school now. BCHS as of 2015 was ahead in technology in most areas. Chromebooks are used effectively to supplement learning. BCHS has a great band and theater program and is the only high school in Merced County to incorporate an engineering academy as an option. The AP teachetrs are the best you will find. AP Chemistry with Camp is the best chemistry you will find in California. The arts are also excellent, Freitas is a personal favorite as well as, Newton go APUSH. Admin is great although I'm sure it has changed since I have left. BCHS strives for school pride and unity. Thy gyms not bad. Overall its the best high school in the area for sure.
my experience in this school is meh

Well im currently a student at buhach and I thoroughly enjoy the school, the staff are great and funny, especially Mr. Freitas, the school is clean and kept up very well, and is also very well organized, my only issue is that recently we students and staff are being required to wear a photo ID at all times and receive a small punishment if found without one, though it is justified with all the craziness going on in the world.

BCHS has a great band and theater program and is the only high school in Merced County to incorporate an engineering academy as an option. The AP teachetrs are the best you will find. AP Chemistry with Camp is the best chemistry you will find in California. The arts are also excellent, Freitas is a personal favorite as well as, Newton go APUSH. Admin is great although I'm sure it has changed since I have left. BCHS strives for school pride and unity. Thy gyms not bad. Overall its the best high school in the area for sure.
my experience in this school is meh

Well im currently a student at buhach and I thoroughly enjoy the school, the staff are great and funny, especially Mr. Freitas, the school is clean and kept up very well, and is also very well organized, my only issue is that recently we students and staff are being required to wear a photo ID at all times and receive a small punishment if found without one, though it is justified with all the craziness going on in the world.

schoolReviews.review: Franklin Elementary School is an exceptional institution that excels in nurturing young minds and fostering a love for learning. The dedicated staff members go above and beyond to create a supportive and engaging environment for students. The school's commitment to academic excellence, coupled with a strong emphasis on character development, sets a remarkable standard for education. With a rich array of extracurricular activities and a focus on individualized attention, Franklin Elementary School truly stands out as a beacon of quality education and holistic growth for every child fortunate enough to be a part of its community.

I would never send my children to this school again. We MOVED out of the school district to get out of the environment. It’s run down (I know school finances are tight). Programs/performances ran by the school are rushed and not organized and there’s hardly any room in the cafeteria to be present for awards and programs (get there an hour early and be prepared to be ambushed by the parents coming in for the next students awards. I’ve never been to a school like this and we’ve been in four elementary schools (we move for work.)

I love this school, it's one of the only reasons I want to stay where I live, so both of my kids can go here. I love all the staff and I go to the Parent Teacher Club meetings and it showed me how much the staff really cares for not only the children but all the families, siblings, and parents, and grandparents. They very caring to the needs of all the children and they do a great job of keeping all the kids safe and well taken care of. I love this school. My daughter loves her class, they really keep the kids busy and learning. She has learned so much!

entryPointFlyout.value:
Wind Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street National Wind Model, which forecasts how hurricanes and costs from resulting wind damages to structures will change over time due to climate change.

A property's Wind Factor indicates its likelihood to experience extreme winds over the next 30 years, from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Wind Factor scores are more likely to experience higher winds more frequently today and in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on the likelihood and speed of hurricane, tornado, or severe storm winds reaching this property, it has minimal wind risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's wind risk is not significantly changing over time.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: This chart shows this property's likelihood of being in a tropical storm event with 3-second wind gusts exceeding 50 mph (39 mph for 1-minute sustained winds) over the next 30 years.

riskFactorHomeURLText.value: See all wind data on firststreet.org

expandableSummary.value: Estimated 80%+ chance of a flood reaching the building in the next 30 years

entryPointFlyout.value:
Flood Factor® is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street Flood Model, a nationwide, probabilistic flood model that shows a location’s risk of flooding from rain, rivers, tides, and storm surge. It builds off of decades of peer-reviewed research and forecasts how flood risks will change over time due to changes in the environment. Flood Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of flood.

A property's Flood Factor is an indicator of its comprehensive flood risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Flood Factors are more likely to have flooded in the past, and are more likely to flood in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on this property’s projected likelihood and depth of flooding, it has severe flood risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's flood risk is not significantly changing over time.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: Flood risk accumulates over time. Cumulative risk is calculated to the largest building or center of an empty lot. Raised or elevated buildings may not be as vulnerable as ground-level buildings or buildings with basements.

entrypointGraphDescription.value: This property has a 99% chance of flooding in the next 30 years.

riskFactorHomeURLText.value: See all flood data on firststreet.org

riskSpecificSubsectionFlyout.value:
The FEMA flood zone shown is the most probable estimated zone.

The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) is a government agency that maps flood zones in communities across the US, identifying areas of varying flood risk on Flood Insurance Rate Maps (FIRMs). FEMA creates FIRMs to inform flood insurance pricing in the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP) and to guide floodplain management regulations for NFIP-participating communities.

riskSpecificSubsectionFlyout2.value: The FEMA flood zone shown is the most probable zone as estimated by MassiveCert, Inc.

riskSpecificSubsectionDescription.value: This property is estimated to be in FEMA Zone AO, which is designated as a high-risk flood area.

insuranceFlyout.value: To help you understand what it costs to protect this home with flood insurance we've partnered with Neptune Flood. Redfin may receive a commission if you purchase a policy through this link. There may be other flood insurance providers in your area.

insuranceDescription.value:

Flood insurance for this home ranges from $848 to $2087 per year, based on information from 6 providers.

entryPointFlyout.value:
Fire Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. It uses the First Street National Wildfire Model's nationwide, behavioral wildfire model that shows a specific location's probabilistic risk of wildfire based on the vegetation, topography, and fire weather in the surrounding area. Fire Factor is not intended to include all possible risks of fire.

A property's Fire Factor indicates its cumulative wildfire risk, ranging from 1 (minimal) to 10 (extreme). Properties with higher Fire Factors are more likely to be in a wildfire in the future.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on this property's distance to wildfire risk areas and burnable vegetation, it has minimal wildfire risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's fire risk is not significantly changing over time.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: Wildfire risk accumulates over time, so a property with a 0.1% chance of wildfire this year would have at least a 3% chance of being affected by wildfire at least once within 30 years. Being affected by wildfire refers to any actively burning fuels coming into contact with the largest building on the property.

entrypointGraphDescription.value: Unlikely to be in a wildfire in next 30 years.

insuranceFlyout.value: Most homeowners insurance typically includes fire coverage but in some areas, this will need to be purchased separately. Investing in fire insurance is one way to offset the cost of wildfire damage, and can help reduce your financial risk.

insuranceDescription.value: Fire insurance for this home ranges from $659 to $1223 per year, based on information from 7 providers.

expandableSummary.value: 7 days above 105° expected this year, 17 days in 30 years

entryPointFlyout.value:
Heat Factor is a tool created by the nonprofit First Street. Heat Factor™ uses the First Street Extreme Heat Model to determine property-specific heat risk across the United States. The model is a spatial temperature model that determines a specific location’s exposure to extreme heat events based on the surface temperature, topography, land cover, and humidity in the surrounding area.

A property's Heat Factor indicates its risk of extreme heat exposure over the next thirty years, ranging from 1 (minimal risk) to 10 (extreme risk). Heat Factors are based on the current average daily high temperature and humidity of a property’s specific location during the hottest month of the year, and considers how it’s expected to grow over the next 30 years.

entryPointDescription.value: Based on current and future temperature and humidity in the area and at this specific location, this property has severe heat risk.

scoreDescription.value: This property's heat risk is increasing as weather patterns change.

entrypointGraphFlyout.value: This chart shows the number of days exceeding what is considered a hot day at this property. This is defined by using the 98th percentile “feels like” temperature in this area, or the hottest 7 days in the 4km area surrounding this property for a given year and using the lowest “high” temperature from those 7 days as a base. A property may have more or less hot days than the surrounding area depending on its individual exposure to heat.

entrypointGraphDescription.value: A “hot day” in this area is considered to be any day with a “feels like” temperature of 105º. Over the next 30 years, this property is expected to see a 10% increase in the number of hot days per year.
